selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: When night comes in the passage, how is the human spirit described?
questions.answer: It is weak, needy, and surrounded by many troubles.

questions.question: What does the person refuse to love in his heart?
questions.answer: Things that fade and disappear.

questions.question: Who does the person turn to for safety and help?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah, the Everlasting One.

questions.question: What does the person ask Allah’s mercy and guidance to do?
questions.answer: To bring light and mend the hurt in his heart.

questions.question: What time does the passage say this prayer is done before?
questions.answer: Before sleep.

questions.question: How is sleep described in a way that teaches a lesson?
questions.answer: It is shown as something like death.

questions.question: Instead of loving weak and dying things too much, who does he stand before in prayer?
questions.answer: He stands before the Eternal One.

questions.question: What takes the place of the things he fears?
questions.answer: Allah’s protection.

questions.question: What happens to a person when he says that he worships Allah alone?
questions.answer: He gains honor through being connected to Allah.

questions.question: What does saying “we ask for help” show about all creation?
questions.answer: All creation needs Allah’s help.

questions.question: What part of the day is the passage talking about?
questions.answer: Nightfall.

questions.question: What is the person’s condition at that time according to the passage?
questions.answer: He is weak, poor, needy, and troubled.

questions.question: Who is the lasting Beloved the person seeks in prayer?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What does he ask Allah to send into his life and future?
questions.answer: Light.

questions.question: What causes wounds in the person’s heart in this passage?
questions.answer: The leaving and loss of creatures and friends.

questions.question: Why is this prayer especially meaningful before bed?
questions.answer: Because bedtime reminds a person of death and the end of the day.

questions.question: Why is the prayer called the last duty of worship in the day?
questions.answer: Because it is done before sleep at the end of the day.

questions.question: Why is praising Allah better than praising needy creatures?
questions.answer: Because Allah is perfect and creatures are not.

questions.question: Who replaces the weak creatures from whom he asks things?
questions.answer: The Powerful and Generous One.

questions.question: What change happens to the worshipper when he remembers the Day of Judgment belongs to Allah?
questions.answer: He rises from smallness to honor through serving Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect the 'Isha prayer with weakness and need?
questions.answer: Because people feel helpless and needy at night.

questions.question: What sentence from Prophet Ibrahim’s story teaches the person not to cling to passing things?
questions.answer: It teaches him not to love what disappears.

questions.question: How can Allah’s mercy help someone whose friends and loved ones are gone?
questions.answer: It can comfort the heart and heal the pain.

questions.question: How will guidance help with the future?
questions.answer: It will make the future bright instead of dark.
